unit: One brake master cylinder (supplied with its fluid reservoir on the examples here) fitted: old unit off the brake booster, new unit bench-bled and fitted, brake lines reconnected, and the brake system bled with new fluid. Not included: the brake booster, the ABS unit, brake lines or hoses, and diagnosis.

finding: There is no live range for this job on the site today (live is null), so this is a first build, not a check. Built totals (parts + stated hours x $120-$160/hr, the national middle labor rate used for these checks): economy 2021 Hyundai Accent about $472-$650 (1.5 hr); midsize 2021 Hyundai Palisade about $413-$569 (1.4 hr); truck 2016 Ford F-150 3.5L EcoBoost about $261-$397 (0.9 hr); luxury 2017 Lincoln Navigator about $282-$423 (1.1 hr). Across the four examples that is roughly $260-$650. Against the benchmarks: the two Hyundai totals overlap the lower part of ThePricer ($450-$950) and YourMechanic's Sentra table ($426-$845) and sit below RepairPal ($656-$796) and Kelley Blue Book ($841-$944); the two Ford totals sit below all four. Two reasons the built totals run low: every labor figure is a warranty time, which is the low end of what a shop bills (RepairPal carries $206-$303 in labor, about 1.3 to 2.5 hours at this rate, against 0.9-1.5 hours here), and the Ford master cylinders list at about $250 where RepairPal carries $450-$493 in parts. A supportable first range is about $260-$650 with a note that shop quotes commonly reach $650-$950. The class order is not what a reader would expect: the pickup and the large luxury SUV come out cheapest because Ford's parts are cheaper and its times shorter, so the classes should be presented as these four examples, not as a rule that economy cars cost more. How solid the labor times are: all four are the maker's own figure for the example vehicle, which is as good as public sources get. The Accent time (1.5 M/H) covers the master cylinder with reservoir, a full bleed and the ABS unit air-bleed. The Palisade time (1.4 M/H) is printed as "Brake oil and master cylinder replacement" and covers draining and refilling the whole system (about 2 liters), which is more fluid work than a plain bleed, so it may be slightly generous for this unit. The two Ford times (0.9 and 1.1 hours) say "includes bench bleed"; an earlier Ford recall for the 2013-2014 F-150 prints the same 0.9 hours as "includes time to bleed brakes", which supports reading the time as covering the bleed, but the 2016-2017 lines do not itemize it. Each class has one stated time, so each hours range is a single number, not a spread. Parts: no aftermarket master cylinder was verified for any of the four examples (one Dorman unit for the F-150 was loaded at $165.26 but its page shows no model years), so every low end is the genuine part at an online discount and every high end is the genuine list price; a quote using an aftermarket or remanufactured unit can be lower on parts. Two cautions on parts: the Palisade prices come from two pages of one seller, and for the F-150 the superseding part number shows a lower list price ($178.36) on two dealer sites whose pages do not name the 2016 truck, so the F-150 high end ($252.73, from the page that does name it) may be about $74 high. What is null and why: nothing is null. Confidence is low because the midsize class rests on one parts seller and each class has a single warranty time. An estimate is never a quote and never a diagnosis.
extras: A quote often adds diagnosis to confirm the master cylinder is the cause, a full brake fluid flush where only a bleed was priced, an ABS unit bleed done with a scan tool, shop supplies, fluid disposal and sales tax. If fluid has leaked from the back of the master cylinder into the brake booster, the booster is usually replaced as well, which adds its own part and about half an hour of labor on the Ford examples (1.4-1.5 hours for both against 0.9-1.1 for the master cylinder alone). A separate reservoir, level sensor or cap where these are not supplied with the new unit, seized or rounded brake line fittings, and brake hoses or lines found damaged during the bleed also add to the bill. Some vehicles use an electronic brake unit that combines the master cylinder with the booster or ABS unit; that is a different and more expensive part than the one priced here.
